title: Bound living Report startup and surface initialization failure
description:
A synthetic production-backed acceptance created the optimization Report Task but did not reach initial Report creation before the local process ended, leaving operators without a cover page during initialization.

Feature: Observable bounded living Report initialization

Scenario: Initial Report publication succeeds
Given an optimization run has created its durable Task
When the Report and initial artifacts are initialized
Then the first Report becomes visible within a bounded startup interval
And the Task identifies the current initialization step

Scenario: Initial publication cannot complete
Given a required GraphQL or artifact request does not complete within its bounded retry policy
When initialization exhausts that policy
Then the Task becomes failed with an actionable startup reason
And no phantom running optimization remains

Scenario: Process ends before Report creation
Given the Report Task exists and no Report has been created
When the worker is interrupted or recovered
Then recovery either resumes the same attempt safely or marks it terminal
And operators can distinguish initialization from portfolio analysis.

No client data, score mutation, schema change, or new infrastructure resource is included.

comments.author: ryan.porter
comments.text: Root cause identified in the living Report service: after Task creation, initialization creates or reads every fixed TaskStage before looking up or creating the Report. Those sequential remote operations create the operator blind interval. Exceptions in stage/report/block setup also occur before the current initialization error boundary, so they can leave a RUNNING Task. Adding outside-in ordering and fail-closed specifications before reordering production code.

comments.author: ryan.porter
comments.text: Implemented and verified the startup repair. New attempts now create the Report before TaskStage/ReportBlock setup and skip the impossible historical-Report lookup; resume attempts still look up their existing Report. Any later stage/block/artifact initialization exception marks the Task failed and updates the already-visible Report with the failure reason. Focused report/portfolio suite passes 50 tests. The completed live score-brief acceptance confirmed the pre-skip path spent roughly 47 seconds in startup work, providing the baseline for the next fresh timing check.

comments.author: ryan.porter
comments.text: Post-fix production-backed acceptance completed safely with no score mutations. Task f5f547f6... and Report b7de78ca... reached terminal completion. The Report was created 0.500 seconds after the living-report Task, proving the new-attempt ordering and skip work. The remaining roughly 40-second blind interval occurred before that Task existed, inside deterministic Task discovery. This should be removed by reusing the procedure's existing Task rather than further optimizing a duplicate-Task lookup.
